bib.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance

question: How can users query paid LLM APIs within a budget while keeping or improving accuracy?
hypothesis: Cheap LLMs answer many queries correctly, and are sometimes right where expensive ones fail, so a learned cascade can cut cost and match or beat the best single LLM.
contributions: Review of the heterogeneous pricing of 12 commercial LLM APIs (Table 1)
Three cost-reduction strategies: prompt adaptation, LLM approximation, LLM cascade
FrugalGPT, an LLM cascade instance, evaluated on HEADLINES, OVERRULING and COQA

method.summary: A cascade of 3 LLM APIs is learned per dataset. A DistilBERT regression scorer rates each answer in [0,1]. An answer is accepted if its score passes a per-stage threshold, otherwise the next API is queried. The list and thresholds are optimised under a cost budget.
method.task: Budget-constrained natural language query answering (classification and reading comprehension) over LLM APIs

datasets.name: HEADLINES
datasets.split: random train/test split, ratio not stated
datasets.source: Sinha and Khandait 2021, financial news, gold price trend (up, down, neutral, none)

datasets.name: OVERRULING
datasets.split: random train/test split, ratio not stated
datasets.source: Zheng et al. 2021, legal sentences, overruling or not

datasets.name: COQA
datasets.split: random train/test split, ratio not stated
datasets.source: Reddy et al. 2019, adapted as direct query answering

models.name: FrugalGPT cascade (length 3)
models.architecture: sequential LLM cascade with scorer and router

other.HEADLINES learned cascade: GPT-J, J1-L, GPT-4 with thresholds 0.96 and 0.37

models.name: DistilBERT regression scorer
models.architecture: DistilBERT with regression head, predicts whether a generation is correct

models.name: 12 LLM APIs: GPT-Curie 6.7B, ChatGPT, GPT-3 175B, GPT-4, J1-Large 7.5B, J1-Grande 17B, J1-Jumbo 178B, Cohere Xlarge 52B, ForeFrontAI QA 16B, GPT-J 6B, FAIRSEQ 13B, GPT-Neox 20B
models.params: 6B to 178B where stated; ChatGPT and GPT-4 NA

training.objective: Scorer: regression on whether a generation is correct. Cascade: maximise E[r(a, f_Lz(q))] subject to average cost <= b, over list L and thresholds tau.

other.router optimiser: specialised optimiser that prunes lists of LLMs with small answer disagreement and approximates the objective by interpolating within a few samples; details not given

inference.prompting: Few-shot prompts with 8 (HEADLINES), 5 (OVERRULING), 2 (COQA) examples; prompt text not given

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct on the test split

metrics.name: Cost
metrics.definition: dollar cost of API calls on the dataset, from March 2023 prices (prompt + generation + per-request)

metrics.name: Cost savings
metrics.definition: cost to reach the best individual LLM's accuracy, FrugalGPT versus that LLM

metrics.name: MPI (maximum performance improvement)
metrics.definition: probability that LLM A is correct while LLM B is wrong

baselines: each of the 12 individual LLM APIs, best being GPT-4 (HEADLINES, OVERRULING) and GPT-3 (COQA)
eval.protocol: Single random train/test split per dataset; no seeds, repeats or significance tests stated.

limits: Needs labeled examples to train the cascade, drawn from the same or similar distribution as test queries.
Learning the cascade costs resources; the authors call it a one-time upfront cost, worthwhile when the query set is larger than the training data.
Only cascade length 3 and three datasets; prompt adaptation and approximation are described but not evaluated.
Latency, fairness, privacy and environmental impact are not measured.
Prices are March 2023 and are dated; train/test split sizes, scorer training details, seeds and optimiser details are not given.
Cost and accuracy compared against the same test set used to evaluate; no variance reported.
Cases remain where all APIs agree but the scorer is unsure, so the whole chain is queried.
